brief: Bad vs Good vs Great pricing — 6 patterns that separate $99 from $9,900 offers.

slots.body: A standalone price is just a number. Great offers anchor value against the cost of inaction or expensive alternatives, making the fee feel trivial by comparison.
slots.note: Always show the premium option first.

slots.body: Good sellers list benefits. Great sellers absorb risk with bold guarantees, transforming the buyer's question from can I afford this to can I afford to wait.
slots.note: The stronger the guarantee, the higher the price.

slots.body: Bad pricing charges for hours and deliverables. Great pricing charges for the transformation, revenue lift, or status gained, never the labor involved.
Open calendars signal desperation. Great offers use limited seats, application filters, or waitlists to frame access as a privilege worth paying premium rates for.
slots.note: Easy to buy is hard to value.

slots.body: One option forces a yes or no. Great pricing presents three tiers where the middle feels sensible and the premium becomes an aspirational anchor.
Bad offers emphasize the expense leaving their wallet. Great pricing frames the fee as capital allocation toward growth, positioning spend as strategic, not indulgent.
Steal these six shifts and watch your next offer convert at prices that finally match your expertise.
